title: DNS-layer security with Umbrella
blurb: Register a network in Cisco Umbrella, block threat categories at the DNS layer, and send the office's DNS to Umbrella.
scenario: The HQ office reaches the Internet from public address **203.0.113.1**. Protect every device in the office, including ones without an agent, by using **Cisco Umbrella** as the DNS resolver. Block malware, phishing and command-and-control domains, and inspect risky domains with the Intelligent Proxy.
topology:
Office clients ── internal DNS ── forwarders → Umbrella 208.67.222.222 / 208.67.220.220
                         egress public IP 203.0.113.1
objectives: Register the office network as an identity
Write a DNS policy with security categories
Point the internal DNS forwarders at Umbrella
Understand how blocking and the Intelligent Proxy work

steps.title: Add the network identity
steps.learn: Umbrella identifies an office by the **public IP** its DNS queries come from. Register that IP as a **Network** identity, and policies can apply to it.
steps.task: Add network **HQ** with IP **203.0.113.1** and prefix **/32**.
steps.screen: Umbrella › Deployments › Core Identities › Networks › Add

steps.title: Create the DNS policy
steps.learn: A **DNS policy** applies security and content settings to the identities it covers. Policies are checked top-down, and the first one that includes the identity applies.
steps.task: Create DNS policy **HQ-Policy** for identity **HQ**. Block the security categories **Malware**, **Phishing Attacks** and **Command and Control Callbacks**, and turn on the **Intelligent Proxy**.

steps.title: Send DNS to Umbrella
steps.learn: Keep the internal DNS servers for local names, and set their **forwarders** to Umbrella's anycast resolvers. Then block outbound DNS (UDP and TCP 53) from everything except those servers, so devices can't bypass Umbrella.
steps.task: Set the forwarders on the internal DNS server to Umbrella's resolvers, and choose the firewall rule that stops bypass.

fields.label: Firewall rule for outbound port 53
options: Allow only from the internal DNS servers, block the rest
fields.answer: Allow only from the internal DNS servers, block the rest

steps.title: What the user sees
steps.question: A user clicks a link to a phishing domain. What does Umbrella do?

options.text: Answers the DNS query with the address of an Umbrella block page, so the browser never connects to the phishing site.
Lets the connection through and scans the page for malware.
options.why: For a domain in a blocked category, Umbrella stops it at the DNS answer, before any connection is made.

options.text: Returns no answer, so the browser shows a timeout.
options.why: Umbrella returns a block page address, so the user sees why the site was blocked.

steps.title: Grey domains
steps.learn: Most domains are clearly safe or clearly malicious. A few, such as file-sharing sites, host both good and bad content.
steps.question: What does the Intelligent Proxy do for a risky domain that isn't outright malicious?

options.text: Answers DNS with the proxy's address, then inspects the full URL and blocks only the bad files or pages on that domain.

options.why: That would block legitimate content too. The proxy checks the URL instead.

options.text: Proxies every domain the office visits.
options.why: Only risky (grey) domains are sent to the proxy. Safe domains resolve normally.

summary: The HQ network identity, a DNS policy blocking malware, phishing and CnC with the Intelligent Proxy turned on, and internal DNS forwarding to Umbrella with port 53 locked down so it can't be bypassed.
